       COMES NOW Walter & Deborah McCullough, (The McCulloughs) pro se intervenors

(Party 645), files their Initial Closing Argument and states as follows.

                                        I.     INTRODUCITON

       The Commission and AJLs should and have the ability and precedence to DENY the Joint

Application per PURA 37.056 (b) (3) of Oncor Electric Delivery Company, LLC (Oncor) and

Lower Colorado River Authory Transmission Service Corporation (LCRA TSC) (collectively, the

Applicants) to Amend their Certificates of Convenience and Necessity (CCN) for the Bell County

East to Big Hill Substation 765-kV Transmission Ling Project in Bell, Burnet, Concho, Coryell,

Lampasas, Llano, Mason, McCullouch, Menard, Milam, Mills, San Saba, Schleicher, Tom Green,

and Williamson Counties (The 59475 Application).

        Additionally, because of SOAH Order 24 (59182) and Order 12 (59475), the Commission

and AJLs should and have the ability and precedence to DENY the Joint Application per PURA

37.056 (b) (3) of Oncor Electric Delivery Company, LLC (Oncor) and Lower Colorado River

Authory Transmission Service Corporation (LCRA TSC) (collectively, the Applicants) to Amend

their Certificates of Convenience and Necessity (CCN) for Big Hill Substation to Sand Lake

Switch 765-kV Transmission Ling Project in Crane, Crockett, Irion, Pecos, Reagan, Reeves,

Schleicher, Tom Green, Upton, and Ward (The 59182 Application).

     The Applicants failed to present factual and accurate data to the evidentiary record, and they

do not demonstrate compliance with the requirements of Public Utility Regulatory Act (PURA)

§37.056 or HB 5066. The Applicants have failed to demonstrate complete evidence on record that

would compel the Public Utility Commission (Commission) to grant the Applicants the supreme

privilege to construct the size and scale of this type of public infrastructure project. Landowners

have not had sufficient time or opportunity to mount a defense of their properties in the 765 KV

cases. Additionally, an approval of this application “will open the door” for further challenges on

the State’s ability to confer eminent domain to private companies, due to the lack of due process

granted in the amended PURA §37.057 by the rapid 180 day approval process being in direct

violation to Landowners Due Course of Law, Due Process and § 2001.051 rights. This would have

far reaching consequences for the state beyond the scope of this project.

                                                                       II.          ARGUMENTS

    A. Certificate of Necessity and Convenience (CCN) applications for Bell County East to Big

           Hill & Big Hill to Sand Lake should have been a consolidated CCN upon application.

        The Applicants have submitted two CCN filings for the one Import Path 2 project. The

Permian Basin Reliability Plan states this fact.1 The CCN 59475 Application is incomplete in that

it points to the CCN Docket 59182 for the Bill Hill Sub-station construction. Neither project can

stand alone without the other CCN and it requires the same Proposal for Decision for each docket,

which renders a congruent or aligned decision in 59182 and 59475 from Administrative Law

Judges reviewing the same information.

        The separation of Import Path 2 into two CCNs allowed the Applicants to drop the least

populated segment of Import 2 CCN 59182 first to force a Proposal for Decision in these

proceedings before 59475, which is a highly populated and contested segment of Import Path 2.

The intent appears to game the system and is harmful to public by benefiting the utility company

and Applicants, which is a monopoly by nature, allowing the Applicants to progress the project to

a “point of no return”. The argument presented by Mr. Kenndey in PUC Docket filing 59182_480

and 59475_3504 points to the basic premise of mandatory consolidation requirements for the

59182 and 59475 dockets.2 This mandatory consolidation has been ordered but only on the “need”

of the project and not a full consolation.3

    Given the PUC STAFF and Applicants have extensive knowledge of PURA rules and

regulations, why did it take the motion of a pro se intervenor, Mr. Kennedy to force the

consolidation that should have occurred from the beginning of these proceedings, due to PURA

statues. Tex Utilities Code §37.0541 states that “The commission shall consolidate the proceeding

 independent report/model backed by a licensed professional engineer through a State issued seal

 pointing to the public need of the project. 7,8 Additionally, there is no evidence that the PUC Staff

 Engineer, Mr. Poole, has completed any independent studies for the project either. 9

 project is needed through his testimony, however he has not published any of his own studies

 Applicant engineer, has not completed or authored any studies with regard to the “need”, which

        C. House Bill 5066

              The Applicants have not completed any engineered studies to justify need as stated in the

 previous argument. Instead, they rely solely on HB 5066 and ERCOT PBRP to point to the need

 of the project.17 As such, since the Applicants relies heavily on HB 5066, one would assume that

 a correct and accurate restatement of the bill and PURA law, would be required as a basis for the

 59475 and 59182 Applications. As stated in cross in 59315 Hearing on Merits, the Applicant

 witness (a witness in 4 PBRP 765 KV dockets) Mr. Gurley answered “Yes” when asked if he is

 well aware of HB 5066 and the language in the bill.18 However, Mr. Gurley and Applicants

 continue to assert HB 5066 requires a transmission only solution to press their agenda for the need

 of Bell County East to Bill Hill and other 765 KV projects.19 This is shown throughout the 765

 KV PBRP Applications (59029, 59182, 59315 and 59475), Applicant witness testimony and

 rebuttal testimony where the directives in HB 5066 are being misrepresented and twisted in front

 of these proceedings, the ALJs, and public in order sway decisions toward a transmission solution

 only.

              Section §39.167 of HB 5066 (b) states without paraphrasing or manipulation that “the plan

 must: 1) address extending transmission service to areas where mineral resources have been found;

 2) address increasing available capacity to meet forecasted load; and 3) provide available

 infrastructure to reduce interconnection times in areas without access to transmission service.”20.

 The actual words in HB 5066 point to very different directives than the representations made by

 Application and Applicant witness Mr. Gurley.

         E. Notice

               The Applicant claims they are compliant with notices, however again they gamed the

 system by splitting up the one Import Path 2 765 KV transmission line into two CCNs 59182 and

 59475.38 Property owners with judiciable interest in the counties on 59475 were not notified about

 the 59182 docket as they will be directly affected by the approval the 59182 (and vice-versa), more

 so than the average rate payer. The record reflects that The McCulloughs were never given proper

 notice about the 59475 CCN docket.

               Additionally, the Applicant added route segments after the summer 2025 public meeting

 which prevented those segment owners from filling out a questionnaire that presents community

 values factors for their specific properties. For 59475 there were 2,809 notices for public meetings

 notices39 sent and 4,215 notices sent for Application.40 This means approximately 1,400 properties

 were unaware until they received their packets several days after application submittal, March 26,
